title: Classes: A Thing That Cannot Be Wrong

questions.question: What is an invariant?
options: Something that is true about an object from creation until destruction
A member that never changes value
A function that cannot be overridden
A constant defined inside a class
questions.explanation: The purpose of a class is to make its invariants impossible to break, using private data and a complete set of operations that each maintain them.

questions.question: Why does making the members private actually help?
options: If the only way to change the object maintains the invariants, they hold after every possible sequence of calls
Private members use less memory
It makes the class faster to compile
It prevents the object from being copied
questions.explanation: The guarantee comes from there being no other route, rather than from everybody remembering to update two fields together.

questions.question: What does const on a member function promise?
options: That the function does not modify the object, checked by the compiler
That the return value cannot be changed
That the function cannot be called twice
That the function has no side effects of any kind
questions.explanation: It also means the object can be passed as a const reference and still be asked questions, which is why an unmarked reading function is annoying to use.

questions.question: Why does Welford's method keep precision where a running total loses it?
options: No quantity ever holds the sum, so the digits are not spent on a large constant offset
It uses long double internally
It divides earlier, which rounds less
It stores every reading and recomputes
questions.explanation: Readings around a million, varying by a hundredth, exhaust a double's significant digits on the constant part. Welford's works in corrections, which stay the size of the variation.

questions.question: A variance comes out negative. What does that tell you?
options: The computation lost precision, since a variance can never be negative
The readings were negative
There were fewer than two readings
The mean was computed incorrectly but the variance is fine
questions.explanation: It is mathematically impossible, so it is a reliable signal that a running total lost the small variations. It is worth asserting on in real code.

questions.question: When is this class the right tool rather than std::accumulate?
options: When readings arrive one at a time and cannot all be kept, which is most of robotics
When the data is already in a vector
When only the mean is needed
When the readings are integers
questions.explanation: The standard algorithms need the whole set at once. An online algorithm folds in one reading at a time and keeps a fixed amount of state forever.
